item.title: Letter to the editor: The feeling Trumpism has arrived in the Territory
item.description: A recent decision by the NT Planning Minister Josh Burgoyne that was not made public, to change some rural area land to allow for smaller blocks, gives the feeling Trumpism has arrived in the Territory, writes Gerry Wood.

item.title: $500,000 reward for information that leads police to Angie Fuller
item.description: The reward for information that leads to police finding missing woman Angie Fuller has been doubled to $500,000, NT Police said.

item.title: Where did Darwin Council’s $125k for city Christmas decorations go?
item.description: Darwin Council will not say if it spent the $126,500 allocated for the annual city Christmas display, that this year involves failing lights, decorations from Christmases long, long ago, and the old Smith Street Christmas tree that appears was only lit for one night.

item.title: Se Acabo: Mirror, mirror on the wall, what has become of us all?
item.description: OPINION: Unlike in the past, none of the exposure following the damning NT Ombudsman's report into the unlawful conditions in our watch houses, and the refusal to let the UN observe, presents any political concerns for the CLP Government who are happy to own it, writes John Lawrence. If anything, it’s seen as a vote winner.

item.title: Police top brass failure to record decisions in Rolfe criminal investigation was ‘unfortunate’ but not misconduct: ICAC
item.description: Police Commissioner Martin Dole told the former head of public prosecutions that Zach Rolfe should be charged with murder over the shooting death of Kumanjayi Walker, but did not have a conflict of interest despite his childhood relationship with the victim’s family, a new ICAC report has found, which also concluded that police management's failure to record major decisions in the case was "unfortunate" and "surprising" but did not amount to improper conduct.

item.title: Andrew Thomas to head Bushfires NT, Reece Kershaw to help find next St John CEO
item.description: The head of ambulance services at the troubled St John Ambulance NT, Andrew Thomas, has been appointed as the new executive director of Bushfires NT, while the ambulance contractor has said it has brought in former Australian Federal Police commissioner Reece Kershaw to help find its next chief executive officer.

item.title: ‘It is just a big joke’: Attorney-General left health complaints review committee dormant
item.description: An Alice Springs man who tried to complain about how the Health and Community Services Complaints Commission handled his health treatment complaint discovered the review committee meant to scrutinise the commission no longer existed, having been left dormant after Attorney-General Marie-Clare Boothby failed to appoint members, while she claimed it would be premature to do so ahead of the establishment of a proposed new integrity body.

item.title: Darwin Waterfront Corporation lost $3.3m last financial year: Report
item.description: The taxpayer-funded Darwin Waterfront Corporation, which was thrust into the public spotlight earlier this year for unresolved governance failures, mismanaged conflicts of interest, and nepotistic hiring practices, ran a record $3.3 million deficit last financial year, while the DWC board's chair appears to have ignored key recommendations to improve the corporation's governance, according to its annual report.

item.title: David Connolly announced as next NT Administrator
item.description: Cattle station manager David Connolly has been announced as the next Administrator of the Northern Territory by Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro, following a period of at least five months in which she said Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would not approve his selection.

item.title: Year in Review 2025: CLP Government’s first full year marred by politics-as-usual in the NT
item.description: It's that time of year again to reflect on the wacky and wonderful stories that made news this year, and in most cases, crucial stories and issues that would never have come to light had the NT Independent not existed. FREE TO READ.
